purpose: A serial overnight queue for this lab. It extends the knowledge table to two more configurations, owns the placement-versus-output check we said we should have, repeats our own instruments under the lab's repeat rule, and takes a second decision model to a second engine. One inference workload at a time; the resource gates are checked between items and the queue stops rather than weakening them; no frozen artifact is edited; a file named OVERNIGHT-STOP in this root cancels the queue before the next item.

items.title: Does the resident budget change the answers?
items.question: The same 93 shared-correct reasoning items run on Strata at --resident-budget-gib 2 and at 8, everything else identical. Every engine now claims identical logits at every cache capacity; this measures ours, and it is the 'placement versus output' instrument this lab argued it should own.
items.prediction: Replies differ on a substantial minority of items (20-60%), because this engine is not seed-stable on long free-form output; the chosen letters change on at most 3 of 93, and the two configurations stay within 2 letters of each other in total correctness.

items.title: A third model on the knowledge instrument
items.question: Kolibri-1 78B (Q3_K_M, its own patched hob-b11434 runtime, experts resident, --load-mode none as declared) on the same 1,100 pinned items as the two leaders. Its results on the coding suite are the best this lab has; nothing is known about its knowledge.
items.prediction: Within 3 points of the two leaders, i.e. 85-92% overall, with GSM8K no worse than MMLU, because the lab's other strong models behave that way.

items.title: The same model on a second engine
items.question: Colibri v2.0.0 serving its own Qwen3.6-35B-A3B build on the same 1,100 items. Same model family as our best configuration, different engine, different quantisation and packing, no GPU required.
items.prediction: Accuracy inside 2 points of our llama.cpp number (88.5%), and the interesting number is wall time per item rather than accuracy.
items.timeout_note: Raised from 7200 on 2026-10-15, declared before the run: measured 45.1 s/item at --cap 32 (65.7 at the engine default), so 1,100 items need ~14 h. The corrected 2026-10-15 attempt answered 86 items in 7200 s before this timeout killed it (exit -9). The item's own wall is 15 h; gates and everything else are unchanged.

items.title: Re-ask what the network dropped
items.question: The 13:23 Colibri run answered a 1,100 items but lost 17 requests to ConnectionResetError 10054 (9 virology, 8 grade-school math), which the strict rule treats as a gap. Are those 17 transport events rather than model answers?
items.prediction: Yes: the fill resolves most of them, lifting the total from 967/1100 toward ~984/1100, and either end leaves accuracy inside 2 points of the llama.cpp 88.5% the i3 prediction named.

items.title: Repeat rule on our own instrument
items.question: The format-fixed 93-item reasoning run, again, both stacks. The lab's rule is that single runs are samples; this is the first repeat of this instrument across runs.
items.prediction: Qwen3.6 90/93 again and Strata 92/93 again, because within a run the replies were byte-identical.

items.title: Repeatability of the free-form form
items.question: Three papers per stack again, same prompt, same pinned sampling. The first run had Qwen3.6 byte-identical three times and Strata producing two different topics.
items.prediction: Qwen3.6 one distinct topic again, Strata two or three.

items.title: A second decision model on a second engine
items.question: GLiNER2.5-Decide on Colibri over the same 18 frozen windows and the same question shape as the Laya replay. Our GLiNER-class verdict was 18/18 correct with 0/4 stalls caught at a 27.56 s p95; Colibri's own speed table predicts 25.7 s at 1923 tokens.
items.prediction: Warm p95 between 20 and 35 s, 0/4 stalls caught, i.e. the latency is the model's sequence-length cost and the detection failure is the model, not the engine.
